subject: How to include smoothing spline for covariate modelling in LGCP

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: How to include smoothing spline for covariate modelling in LGCP
parts:
Hi,

I have been reading about the following paper:  Accounting for preferential sampling in species distribution models by Pennino et al. 

In their model construction, they mentioned using a Bayesian smoothing spline to model the nonlinear effect of the covariate. I am trying to do a similar thing for my problem but I am not exactly sure how to incorporate a smoothing spline for the covariates in my model. Mostly, I am not familiar with the syntax and there does not seem to be any example code online for doing this.

Can someone provide any help for this? Thank you very much!

Best,
David

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to include smoothing spline for covariate modelling in LGCP
parts:
Use a rw2 model, which is the continuous Bayesian process model linked to the spline penalty given by the integral of the squared second order derivative. Most inla examples with nonlinear covariate effects use that model, so there should be plenty of examples.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to include smoothing spline for covariate modelling in LGCP
parts:
Step 1 should be to make sure that you're setting a sensible prior. with scale.model=TRUE and a PC-prior for the standard deviation, you control the prior for the (geometric) average std.dev.

Limiting the number of knots to intentionally get an oversmoothed estimate  is a bit of a hack, but you can do something similar by using a 1D spde with 2nd order basis functions; inla.mesh.1d(knots, degree = 2, boundary = "free") with inla.sdpe2.pcmatern() has both a range a nd std.dev parameter, but if needed you can fix the range (with prior.range=c(fixedrange, NA))

I have the impression that models where rw2 models overfit are rather due to other problems with those problems, or misinterpretation of the results.
In cases where rw2 models really aren't smooth enough, the more appropriate solution should be to use a rw3 or rw4 model instead. (can be done via generic, but I haven't tried it)

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to include smoothing spline for covariate modelling in LGCP
parts:
I don't have any general advice for prior choice unfortunately, as it can be very problem specific; consider the likely scale of the effect, and set the std.dev. prior accordingly. I think the PC-prior paper may discuss that. Also see the Matern PC-prior paper, at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1503.00256.pdf

Finn
